docs.title: timescales (Python)
docs.text:
Python binding of the R package timescales: calendars and timeslices for modeling, built on nestedscales. A calendar is a nested partition of a model year (months, days, hours, weeks, seasons, fiscal years, representative hours); data is converted between calendars through the datetime grid of a year.

import pyarrow as pa
import timescales as ts

m12, q4 = ts.calendar("m12"), ts.calendar("q4")
d = pa.table({"timeslice": ts.calendar_timeslices(m12),
              "energy": [float(i) for i in range(1, 13)]})
ts.recast_calendar(d, m12, q4, year=2021, rule="sum")

cal = ts.calendar("d365_h24")
ts.datetime_to_timeslice(ts.base_calendar(2021)["datetime"][:3], cal)
ts.tsl2month(["d032_h00"], cal)

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Ported: tokens and the 43-design catalog, calendar() / calendar_build() / calendar_from_leaftable(), navigation and queries, filter_calendar() / prune_calendar(), the datetime engine (base_calendar, expand_calendar, datetime_to_timeslice, as_timeframe), calendar_map() / calendar_map_between(), recast_calendar() (including the share rules), recast_to_timebase() / recast_from_timebase(), join_calendar(), and the timeslice conversions (tsl2*, dtm2tsl, hour2HOUR, yday2YDAY). Plotting (calendar_plot, geom_calendar, wall layouts) stays in R.

Function names match R. As agreed for the whole stack, R's from/to arguments are source/target (R renames them in its next release), and the clear_* functions take name. Error and warning messages are R's.

Datetimes are pyarrow timestamps (or numpy, pandas, polars, Python datetimes); fields are read in the array's time zone with lubridate's conventions. Data may be pyarrow, pandas, polars or a lazy pyarrow Dataset / polars LazyFrame, and results come back in the caller's type.

as_calendar() restores a Calendar from a scale reopened with nestedscales.open_scale_dataset().

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text: The R package is the original implementation. This Python binding was translated from it with the AI coding assistant Claude Code, function by function, and is checked against results generated from the R sources (see Verification below). Human review and contributions are very welcome; issues and pull requests go to https://github.com/optimal2050/timescales.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• specs/golden/ -- the language-neutral cases the R suite also replays;
  • specs/json/ -- a broad set written by tools/specs/make_json_goldens.R from the R sources (with nestedscales as submitted to CRAN): every catalog calendar, datetime labelling across leap years, fiscal anchors, UTC offsets and time zones, crosswalks, every recast rule, navigation, joins and conversions, with warning and error text.
python -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -e "../../nestedscales/python" -e ".[test]" pyyaml
.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q
Rscript tools/specs/make_json_goldens.R      # from the repository root

docs.title: calendar_from_leaftable
docs.text:
calendar_from_leaftable(
    leaftable: Any,
    timeframes: Sequence[str] | str,
    members: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]] | None = None,
    name: str = "",
    desc: str = "",
    year_start: Mapping | None = None,
    utc_offset_minutes: int = 0,
    year_fraction: float = 1,
    row_order: str = "nested",
    **meta: Any,
) -> Calendar

Build a Calendar from a table with one row per leaf timeslice.

timeslice defaults to the timeframe labels joined with "_", weight to share * 8760, and members to first-appearance order. Extra keyword arguments become meta entries.

docs.title: calendar_build
docs.text:
calendar_build(
    *tokens: str,
    name: str | None = None,
    desc: str = "",
    year_start: Mapping | None = None,
    utc_offset_minutes: int = 0,
    year_fraction: float = 1,
    **meta: Any,
) -> Calendar

A calendar as the Cartesian product of tokens, coarsest first.

Shares are year_fraction times the product of the token shares; the rows run in nested, chronological order: coarsest timeframe first. A nontrivial year_start rotates the MONTH/QUARTER member order.

docs.title: as_timeframe
docs.text:
as_timeframe(
    x: Any,
    timeframe: str,
    format: Literal["numeric", "token"] = "numeric",
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> list

Read one timeframe off datetimes, timeslice labels, or numbers.

  • datetimes: the field in the datetimes' time zone (week_start= for WDAY/MWEEK);
  • timeslice labels: read from calendar= (a Calendar or a name) by a join, never by parsing the label text; year= for the weekday-derived timeframes;
  • numbers: format="token" spells them with the calendar's vocabulary (calendar=) or the canonical formatter.

The leaf timeslice each datetime falls in (None where none does).

The calendar's utc_offset_minutes shifts the instants first; year_start anchors YDAY and YEAR. alignment overrides how instants beyond a vocabulary map (one rule, or a mapping per timeframe).

docs.title: recast_calendar
docs.text:
recast_calendar(
    x: Any,
    source: Calendar,
    target: Calendar | str,
    year: int,
    key: str | None = None,
    values: Any = None,
    rule: str | None = None,
    by: object = None,
    tz: str = "UTC",
    na_action: NaAction = "drop",
    parent: Calendar | str | None = None,
    collect: bool | None = None,
) -> Any

Recast timeslice data from one calendar to another (or to a timeframe of the same calendar) through the datetime grid of year.

Columns other than the key and the values are identifiers. rule is one of CALENDAR_RULES, or None to use register_calendar_rule(). Rule "share" keeps the source key and returns shares within parent.

docs.title: recast
docs.text:
recast_calendar() and the timebase halves (port of R/recast.R).

Every conversion routes source -> datetime grid -> target. The route is collapsed into a crosswalk by calendar_map_between(), and the aggregation is nestedscales' recast_crosswalk(), so NA semantics (including the partial-source law) are the core's.
